chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Ibrahim, the son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), was taken (died), three customs were established. As for one of them: when he died, the sun was eclipsed, and the people said, "The sun was eclipsed due to the loss of the son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)." So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said, "O people, the sun and the moon are two signs among the signs of Allah; they move by His command, obedient to Him. They do not eclipse for the death of anyone or for their life. So when they eclipse, or one of them, pray." Then he descended and led the people in the prayer of the eclipse.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and significance of the solar eclipse prayer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) narrates the event of the solar eclipse during the death of Prophet Muhammad's son, Ibrahim, establishing the Sunnah that the eclipse is a natural sign of Allah, not caused by the death or birth of a person, and prescribes the ritual prayer (Salat al-Kusuf) as the response to this phenomenon. In Shia scholarship, this narration is pivotal for distinguishing between the cosmic signs (Ayat) and superstitious beliefs, emphasizing that celestial movements are independent of human events. It also highlights the Prophet's practical leadership in guiding the community through communal worship during natural phenomena, reinforcing the spiritual significance of Salat al-Ayat.
